text: Every object you manage in a tenant starts with the user. A cloud-only account is created directly in Entra ID and lives only there. A synced account originates in an on-prem Active Directory and is mirrored in by Microsoft Entra Connect. We're focusing on cloud-only here, but most mid-size and large organizations actually run a hybrid setup, with both kinds of accounts side by side.

Entra ID has two group types, and picking the wrong one is a common early mistake. A security group exists purely to grant access — to resources, apps, or Azure RBAC roles, which is Lesson 7. A Microsoft 365 group is broader: creating one also provisions a shared mailbox, a calendar, a Teams channel, and a SharePoint site. Need a shared workspace, use a Microsoft 365 group. Need to grant access, use a security group.

A license isn't a login credential — it's what turns on specific services for a user who already has an account. Assigning Microsoft 365 E3 unlocks Exchange Online, Teams, and SharePoint. Assigning Entra ID P1 unlocks premium identity features like Conditional Access and dynamic groups. No license, no access to that service, even though the account itself still exists and can sign in.

Both group types can use static membership, where you manually add and remove people, or dynamic membership, where Entra ID evaluates a rule against each user's attributes automatically. A rule like department equals Finance adds anyone with that attribute and removes them the moment it changes — nobody has to remember to update membership by hand. Licenses can also be assigned to a group instead of a user, so every member inherits it automatically as they join or leave.

Put those together and the whole lifecycle runs itself: Dana joins Finance, her department attribute gets set, the dynamic Finance group picks her up automatically, and the Microsoft 365 E3 and Entra ID P1 licenses already attached to that group apply within minutes — zero manual tickets. Next up: turning those same security groups into real permissions with Azure RBAC.
